rationale: A ribbon entering the heart creates a false notch when visible-paper segmentation treats the occluded region as exposed background. Existing scene variants forbid overlap with the selected body.
selection: Use the existing ForegroundCorpus experimentalSplit, not merely parent split=train. First sixteen distinct training geometry hashes in lexical order, one deterministically chosen original view each. No real photograph, QA source, development geometry or recipe holdout enters this pilot.
generation: Superimpose a projected foreground ribbon crossing the known notch into the overlap. Vary width, length and colour deterministically. Keep original views and all latent cutting geometry/camera labels unchanged. New output directory only.

labels.amodalBody: Original complete synthetic paper occupancy from the fixed known camera and geometry.
labels.visibleBody: Physical paper occupancy multiplied by unoccluded coverage.
labels.occludedBody: Physical paper occupancy multiplied by occluder coverage.
labels.occluderCoverage: Known foreground object coverage, distinct from background.
labels.materialObservation: Original photograph support multiplied by unoccluded coverage; hidden paper labels must not be scored as observed.
labels.originalMaterialAndCuts: Preserved latent references, not inferred from new occluded RGB.

verification: Check visibleBody + occludedBody equals amodalBody, including fractional edge coverage.
Verify image compositing, all original source/camera/geometry identities and group isolation.
Require each generated ribbon to actually occlude some paper and include the notch neighbourhood.
Inspect all sixteen source/occluded/visible/amodal/observation panels before any training.
Keep counts of source geometries and augmented views separate.
A small raster-composite pilot is not a physically calibrated photographic simulation.
Do not train or integrate a model merely because the synthetic labels are consistent; declare the training comparison separately.
